title: Recurrent axillary nodules with sinus tracts: hidradenitis suppurativa (follicular occlusion)
vignette: A 45-year-old man comes to the office due to recurrent, painful skin lesions in the right axilla for the past 6 months. The patient has no other medical history and takes no medication. He smokes a pack of cigarettes every day and works as a roofer. Vital signs are normal. Examination reveals tender, subcutaneous nodules in the right axilla along with interconnecting sinus tracts and double (bridged) comedones. The remainder of the examination is normal. Which of the following is the most likely cause of the condition?

clues.text: recurrent, painful skin lesions in the right axilla for the past 6 months
clues.note: Chronic, recurrent, painful lesions in an intertriginous site (axilla) are characteristic of hidradenitis suppurativa; tobacco use is a risk factor.

clues.text: tender, subcutaneous nodules in the right axilla
clues.note: Deep-seated, painful subcutaneous nodules in the axilla (or groin/inframammary/perineal folds) are the primary lesions of hidradenitis suppurativa.

clues.text: interconnecting sinus tracts and double (bridged) comedones
clues.note: Draining sinus tracts and double (bridged) comedones are hallmark chronic findings of hidradenitis suppurativa and follow follicular rupture.

whatMatters: Recurrent, painful AXILLARY nodules with SINUS TRACTS and double comedones = HIDRADENITIS SUPPURATIVA. It begins with OCCLUSION of FOLLICULOPILOSEBACEOUS UNITS (keratinocyte hyperproliferation) -> follicular rupture -> inflammation, abscesses, sinus tracts, and scarring. Answer D.
strategy: Recognize hidradenitis suppurativa (recurrent intertriginous nodules/abscesses/sinus tracts/scarring) and recall its INITIATING lesion: occlusion of the folliculopilosebaceous unit (not an infection of sweat glands). Reject eccrine gland bacterial infection (older, disproven 'sweat gland' theory), Cutibacterium acnes immune response (acne vulgaris - face/chest, adolescents), and malignant transformation (squamous cell carcinoma - a rare late complication with a scaly plaque, not the cause).

options.text: Bacterial proliferation in eccrine sweat glands

eliminations.label: Eccrine sweat gland infection - outdated theory
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: the old idea that hidradenitis is a primary infection of apocrine/eccrine SWEAT glands. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: current understanding attributes HS to FOLLICULAR (folliculopilosebaceous) occlusion, not a primary sweat-gland infection. ✅ Correct if: a true eccrine gland disorder (not HS).

eliminations.label: Cutibacterium acnes immune response - acne vulgaris
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: follicular colonization by C acnes driving acne vulgaris. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: acne vulgaris affects the face/chest/upper back in adolescents; HS involves intertriginous regions (axilla/groin) after puberty and is not primarily driven by C acnes. ✅ Correct if: comedones/papulopustules of acne vulgaris.

eliminations.label: Malignant transformation - rare late complication, not cause
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: squamous cell carcinoma arising in chronically inflamed skin. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: SCC is a rare LATE complication of long-standing HS and appears as a well-demarcated scaly plaque - it is not the CAUSE of the recurrent nodules. ✅ Correct if: a chronic HS lesion developing a persistent scaly plaque/ulcer (biopsy).

reasoning: Recurrent painful axillary nodules with sinus tracts/comedones = hidradenitis suppurativa
HS begins with occlusion of the folliculopilosebaceous unit (keratinocyte hyperproliferation)
Follicular rupture releases contents, causing inflammation, abscesses, sinus tracts, and scarring
-> obstruction of folliculopilosebaceous units; answer D
mechanism: HIDRADENITIS SUPPURATIVA (HS) is a chronic, recurrent inflammatory skin disorder of intertriginous (apocrine-gland-bearing) areas - AXILLAE, groin, inframammary folds, and perineum. Despite its name, it is NOT a primary sweat-gland infection; its pathogenesis begins with OCCLUSION of the FOLLICULOPILOSEBACEOUS UNIT due to keratinocyte hyperproliferation and abnormal differentiation. Mechanical stress/friction in skin folds then causes FOLLICULAR RUPTURE and release of proinflammatory contents, producing painful deep nodules, DRAINING ABSCESSES, epithelialized SINUS TRACTS, double (bridged) COMEDONES, and extensive FIBROSIS/scarring. Contributing factors include tobacco use, obesity, hormonal (androgen) effects, and secondary bacterial colonization. Unlike common furuncles that resolve with drainage/antibiotics, HS persists and recurs over months to years. The distractors are the outdated sweat-gland theory, acne vulgaris (C acnes), and squamous cell carcinoma (a rare late complication, not the cause).

difficulty.label: 🧠 Knowledge
difficulty.text: First Aid Derm > hidradenitis suppurativa: follicular occlusion of folliculopilosebaceous units -> rupture, abscesses, sinus tracts, comedones, scarring; intertriginous sites; smoking/obesity/androgens; chronic/recurrent; SCC risk late.

difficulty.label: 📖 Comprehension
difficulty.text: Recurrent axillary nodules + sinus tracts = HS; root cause is follicular (folliculopilosebaceous) occlusion.

difficulty.label: 🔤 Vocab
difficulty.text: Unsure on hidradenitis suppurativa, folliculopilosebaceous unit, sinus tract, double comedone, or intertriginous? Tell me which.

difficulty.label: 🨤 Distractor
difficulty.text: Sweat-gland infection is the outdated theory; C acnes = acne vulgaris; malignant transformation is a rare late complication, not the cause.

difficulty.label: 🖼️ Imaging / diagram
difficulty.text: Skin exam/exhibit: axillary tender nodules with interconnecting sinus tracts and double (bridged) comedones = hidradenitis suppurativa (follicular occlusion).

difficulty.label: 🗒️ Other
difficulty.text: Bank: hidradenitis suppurativa = follicular (folliculopilosebaceous) occlusion in intertriginous skin -> abscesses, sinus tracts, scarring.

keywords.back: Occlusion of folliculopilosebaceous units (not sweat glands)
Draining abscesses, sinus tracts, double comedones, scarring
Squamous cell carcinoma in chronic lesions

firstAid.detail: Derm: follicular occlusion -> rupture, sinus tracts, scarring in skin folds.
Derm > not eccrine infection; not primarily C acnes.

memoryHook: Hidradenitis 'suppurativa' sounds like sweat glands, but it's really clogged HAIR follicles in the armpit/groin that burst into tunnels (sinus tracts) and scars.
